title: Brownian Motion
description: Pollen grains in water never keep still. In 1905 Einstein showed why, molecules too small to see, striking them at random, and how far they wander says how big the molecules are. Perrin watched, and atoms were real. Unlocks the Brownian Microscope.

puzzle.goal: A sphere of radius r drifts through a liquid of viscosity η at temperature T. The drag of the liquid and the random kicks of its molecules are two sides of one thing; write the sphere's diffusion coefficient D from the thermal energy scale k _ B T.
puzzle.name: Stokes-Einstein relation
puzzle.form: k _ B * T / ( 6 * π * η * r )
puzzle.ask: Find D in µm²/s for a clay grain of r = @{r} m in water at T = @{T} K (n = @{n} Pa·s, k = 1.381e-23 J/K).
puzzle.method: A force F drags the sphere at F/(6πηr) (Stokes); in equilibrium the drift down a concentration gradient balances the diffusion up it, so D = kT × that mobility.
